title: P1 · The health check and the choice to share
description: Three months before Hajj, Kamal has the mandatory pre-Hajj health examination with Dr Aisyah. He is fit to travel. She explains what the Hajj Health Record is, who can see it, and for how long. Kamal agrees on his wallet to share his patient summary with Saudi health workers during Hajj, and sets how the link to it is protected. Step 1 of the overview of key process flows.
where: A GP clinic in Kuala Terengganu

illustrationStyle.prompt: Warm, flat digital illustration with soft shading and clean outlines, friendly and respectful, in the style of a public-health storybook. Wide banner, aspect ratio 11:4. Bright natural daylight, soft pastel palette with clear colour accents. Faces in gentle three-quarter view with expressive, kind features. Technology shown as simple, oversized icons: a phone with a QR code, a shield with a check mark, a small speech bubble with a symbol. No readable text, no logos, no real brands, no flags with text. All people are fictional.

cast.description: Malaysian man, 61, slim, short grey hair, kind face. Batik shirt in Malaysia. In KSA, white two-piece ihram (unstitched towelling cloth, right shoulder bare when in ihram), a small waist pouch and one phone.
His wife, about 58. White modest Hajj outfit and white telekung-style hijab in KSA; pastel baju kurung and tudung in Malaysia.
Malaysian GP, late 30s, tudung, white coat.

notes: Ihram (two white unstitched sheets) is for men only; women wear ordinary modest clothing, usually white, face and hands uncovered.
Keep the Kaaba and other holy sites far in the background or out of frame.
Keep medical signs text-free so generators don't invent wrong Arabic.
The picture carries no text: the step title and the caption are page text.

steps.title: The health check and the choice to share
steps.headline: Kamal is found fit to travel, hears who can see his Hajj Health Record and for how long, and agrees on his wallet to share it.
steps.where: A GP clinic in Kuala Terengganu
steps.touchpoint: Pre-Hajj health examination; consent on the wallet
steps.narrative: Three months before Hajj, Kamal has the mandatory pre-Hajj health examination with Dr Aisyah. He is fit to travel. She explains what the Hajj Health Record is, who can see it, and for how long. Kamal agrees on his wallet to share his patient summary with Saudi health workers during Hajj, and sets how the link to it is protected. Step 1 of the overview of key process flows.

experiences.doing: Has his health examination, listens to Dr Aisyah, and confirms on his wallet that Saudi health workers may see his summary during Hajj; sets how the link is protected.
experiences.feeling: “So the doctors there will know about my insulin. Good.”

experiences.doing: Examines Kamal, finds him fit to travel, and explains what the record is, who can see it and for how long.
experiences.feeling: “He understood what he agreed to. That is what matters.”

experiences.doing: Shows the consent form and the link's privacy settings, and sends the consent to the HIE.

steps.painPoint: Without consent recorded at home, nothing may be shared abroad, and the clinic in Mina starts from nothing.
steps.enabler: Consent is given with a clinician who can explain it, and confirmed by the pilgrim on his own phone.
steps.policy: Is consent given once for the whole Hajj season, per facility, or per encounter — and can Kamal withdraw it while abroad?

handoff.summary: Kamal's consent is recorded at home

illustration.prompt: A bright clinic room in Kuala Terengganu, window showing palm trees and a coastal town. Dr Aisyah sits beside Kamal (batik shirt), who holds his phone; Salmah sits next to him. The phone shows a large consent screen with a check-mark toggle and a small padlock. Dr Aisyah gestures to a simple card with shield, eye and calendar icons (who can see it, for how long). Kamal smiles, reassured.
